title: Local-hire outcomes at comparable large developments
notes: Evidence base for the Universal resort at Kempston Hardwick (opening 2031, ~8,050 operational jobs). Every figure below was read in the cited page or PDF on the retrieval date. 'Local' is defined very differently across cases (host/growth boroughs, a single borough, a 15-mile radius, a county, a French departement), so shares are not directly comparable: wider definitions mechanically give higher shares. Patterns: (1) construction workforces land at roughly 15-30% local when 'local' is a group of host boroughs inside a big labour market (London 2012 ODA 17.5-27%, LLDC parkwide 14% vs 30% target); (2) operational workforces of resort/leisure sites in less dense areas reach 90%+ when local is a county or 15-mile radius (Center Parcs Woburn Forest 90%, Eden Project 91%); (3) a single inner-London borough captures roughly 20-30% of a large operational site's jobs (Westfield Stratford ~1 in 5 Newham residents by 2018; Battersea 29.3% Wandsworth+Lambeth); (4) local share rises over time as staff relocate near the site (Disneyland Paris: 32% of employees lived in Seine-et-Marne at opening in 1992, 67% by 2008, 73% by 2017). Several opening-period figures are operator or council statements rather than audited outcomes; see each note.

entries.development: London 2012 Olympic Park and Athletes' Village construction (Olympic Delivery Authority)
entries.location: Stratford, east London (five host boroughs: Newham, Tower Hamlets, Hackney, Waltham Forest, Greenwich)
entries.target: At least 15 per cent of the construction workforce to be residents of the host boroughs
entries.achieved: Olympic Park: 5,241 of 29,750 contractor workers (17.5%) lived in the host boroughs, 2008-2011; 10.2% previously unemployed. Athletes' Village: 4,507 of 16,548 (27.2%) host-borough residents, 2010-2011
entries.source_title: Report 5: Post-Games Evaluation, Meta-Evaluation of the Impacts and Legacy of the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games, East London Evidence Base (Grant Thornton et al. for DCMS, July 2013), Figure 4-3
entries.note: jobs = cumulative headcount of workers who passed through Olympic Park contractors, not FTE. Target of 15% from DCMS news story 'London 2012 Games construction on track thanks to 12,000-strong workforce' (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/2012-games-construction-on-track-thanks-to-12-000-strong-workforce), which also reported 'nearly a quarter' of the 12,112 then on site lived in the host boroughs. Point-in-time snapshots ran higher (about a quarter) than the cumulative 17.5% for the Park.

entries.development: London 2012 Games-time workforce (LOCOG staff and contractors)
entries.location: London; six host boroughs (Newham, Tower Hamlets, Hackney, Waltham Forest, Greenwich, Barking and Dagenham)
entries.local_definition: Resident in the six host boroughs
entries.target: "We have been committed to recruiting 15-20 per cent of our workforce from the six Host Boroughs" (Seb Coe, LOCOG chair, May 2012)
entries.achieved: LOCOG Games-time workforce: 1,951 of 8,300 (23.5%) host-borough residents, 55% of whom were previously workless. LOCOG contractor workforce: 21,000 of 100,000 (21%) host-borough residents; 7,140 (34%) previously workless
entries.source_title: Report 5: Post-Games Evaluation, East London Evidence Base (DCMS, July 2013), Figure 4-3; target from GLA press release, 17 May 2012
entries.note: Target source: https://www.london.gov.uk/press-releases-4721. Temporary event jobs, not permanent posts. Contractor share by sector ranged from 21% (retail) to 44% (traffic management). The most closely comparable operational benchmark for a hospitality and visitor-attraction workforce.

entries.development: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park legacy operations and construction (London Legacy Development Corporation)
entries.local_definition: Resident of the four growth boroughs
entries.target: Contractual: 50% (estates and facilities management, idverde), 55% (London Aquatics Centre, Everyone Active), 60% (Copper Box Arena, GLL); parkwide construction 30%
entries.achieved: Estates/FM 42% (Nov 2024); London Aquatics Centre 62% (Dec 2024); Copper Box Arena 86%; parkwide construction 14% (Jan 2025)
entries.source_title: LLDC Regeneration and Communities Committee, Appendix 1: Regeneration reporting
entries.note: Venue operator workforces are small (tens to low hundreds); the same paper counts 11,830 end-use jobs across the Park but does not report a local share for them. Construction underperformance blamed on East Bank packages reaching completion. Shows contractual local-labour targets of 50-60% are achievable for operational leisure staff, but construction targets were missed.

entries.local_definition: Newham residents (some measures restricted to unemployed Newham residents)
entries.target: "10,000 permanent jobs have been created, 2,000 of which were put in place for the long-term local unemployed" (Retail Gazette, 13 Sep 2012)
entries.achieved: "Of the 10,000 permanent jobs created to operate Westfield Stratford City, around 3,000 have gone to unemployed Newham residents" (DCMS Report 5, 2013). Newham Partnership minutes, 6 Dec 2011: "2,200 residents were working at Westfield Stratford City, with 48% of these individuals being under 25"; a councillor cited "45% of jobs at Westfield going to Newham residents"
entries.source_title: Report 5: Post-Games Evaluation, East London Evidence Base (DCMS, July 2013), citing London Borough of Newham
entries.note: Also opened: https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2012/09/20444-westfield-stratford-attracts-47m-shoppers-in-first-year/ (2,000 target wording) and https://opencouncil.network/meetings/129330 (Newham Partnership Employment and Enterprise Partnership Action Board, 6 Dec 2011). DCMS: 2,000-3,000 equals 20-30% of the jobs, delivered through Newham's Workplace brokerage and the Skills Place retail academy with guaranteed interviews from John Lewis, Waitrose, M&S and Vue. The councillor's 45% claim is unsourced. On construction, Volterra (via DCMS) estimated 20% of construction jobs were in East London. A government news story of 9 May 2012 reported more than 3,000 trained residents employed at Westfield (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/minister-experiences-the-skills-and-jobs-legacy-that-will-benefit-stratford).

entries.local_definition: Employees living in the London Borough of Newham
entries.achieved: "one in five Westfield Stratford City employees live in the local London Borough of Newham"; centre supports 13 per cent of all jobs in Newham
entries.source_title: Retail Gazette, 'Westfield Stratford breaks footfall records with 50m annual visitors' (27 Nov 2018), reporting Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield's '10 Years in the Making' report
entries.note: Secondary report of an operator study; the underlying URW report was not opened. About 20% residence share across all staff, below the 20-30% of opening jobs that went to Newham residents, which suggests churn and a drift towards wider commuting once opening-period brokerage ends.

entries.location: Nine Elms, London Borough of Wandsworth
entries.target: Local Employment Agreement with Wandsworth Council (construction skills and employment targets, reported as 'met or exceeded' for completed phases); no numerical operational target stated in the report
entries.achieved: "29.3% of the operational workforce at BPS are local residents"; 1,091 jobs filled by BASE since 2017; 641 construction roles secured by local people
entries.source_title: Battersea Power Station, Generating Opportunities: Local Employment Agreement Annual Report 2025/26
entries.note: Operator-published monitoring under a council agreement. 7,500 people work across the estate (retail, leisure and offices, including Apple). Brokerage is through BASE (Battersea Academy for Skills and Employment) with Wandsworth Work Match. Mixed-use site, so not a pure leisure workforce.

entries.local_definition: Living within 15 miles of the site
entries.achieved: "we have recruited and trained 1,500 employees, 40% of whom are within the 16-24 age range and 90% live within 15 miles"
entries.source_title: Center Parcs press release, 'New Center Parcs village now open to short break guests' (5 June 2014)
entries.note: Closest geographical comparator: roughly 5-6 miles from Kempston Hardwick, in the same labour market (Bedford, Milton Keynes, Central Bedfordshire). Operator claim at opening, not independently monitored. Quote typos in the release ('receruited', 'ager') are silently corrected. The workforce is about 1/5 the size of the Universal resort's.

entries.development: Disneyland Paris (Euro Disney) and Val d'Europe
entries.local_definition: Employees housed in the Seine-et-Marne departement (wider measure: Seine-et-Marne, adjacent departements and Paris)
entries.target: No numeric local-hire target found; governed by the 1987 State-Euro Disney convention (public-private partnership)
entries.achieved: "La proportion des employes loges en Seine et Marne a plus que double depuis l'ouverture, passant de 32% (1/3) en 1992 a 67% (2/3) en 2008. La quasi totalite (88%) loge desormais en Seine et Marne ou dans les Departements limitrophes et Paris." The 2017 figure was 73% living in Seine-et-Marne and 17% in Val d'Europe
entries.source_title: Delegation Interministerielle au projet Euro Disney, 'Disneyland Paris, Etude d'impact economique et social: Bilan 2008' (16 Dec 2009)
entries.note: This measures where employees live, not hiring of pre-existing residents, so it captures in-migration and new housing at Val d'Europe as well as local recruitment. 2017 figures (73% / 17%, 15,000 Cast Members) are from DLP Town Square's summary of Disneyland Paris's report '25 ans de contribution economique et sociale' (Feb 2017): https://dlptownsquare.com/30-years-convention-disneyland-paris. The 15,000 headcount is also confirmed by the Prefecture d'Ile-de-France release of 1 June 2016. Strongest analogue for a large destination resort: the local share started low (one third) and doubled over 16 years as housing was built nearby.

entries.achieved: "91% of Eden's staff live in Cornwall" (average of 430 FTE directly employed a year, 2001-2026)
entries.source_title: Eden Project Impact Report (25th anniversary, March 2026; analysis by Counter Culture)
entries.note: A visitor attraction in a peripheral county labour market with little commuting from outside. The county-wide definition (Cornwall, population about 570k) is much broader than a borough. Workforce is roughly 1/20 the size of the Universal resort's.
